macro: This newsletter is a single-company earnings note rather than a broad market overview. No index moves, risk tone, or overnight macro context is provided. The focus is entirely on SpaceX's Q3 results released after the close on October 20, 2026.
market_outlook: No broad directional market view is offered. The key catalyst to watch is Elon Musk's commentary on the SpaceX earnings call, which is expected to matter far more to investors than the headline Q3 numbers themselves.
bull_case: SpaceX delivered a massive Q3 revenue beat of $14.6B vs. the Street's $12.8B, and EBITDA of $8.8B crushed the $6.6B consensus. The Super Intelligence business grew 830% year-over-year, fueled by new cloud services agreements, the Cursor acquisition, and surging Grok adoption. Compute capacity hit 1.7GW and the company signed additional cloud contracts in the quarter.
bear_case: Expectations were already elevated heading into the print, so the beat may be partially priced in. Connectivity subscriber numbers missed at 13.6 million versus the 14.2 million consensus, raising questions about saturation. Investors are more focused on forward-looking topics — compute capacity targets, ARR goals, Starlink Mobile viability, and Tesla merger speculation — and any disappointment on those fronts on the call could pressure the stock.

company_items.summary: SpaceX reported Q3 revenue of $14.6B, up 161% year-over-year and well above the Street's $12.8B estimate, with EBITDA of $8.8B versus consensus of $6.6B. The Super Intelligence segment was the standout, growing 830% driven by new cloud services agreements, the Cursor acquisition, and Grok adoption. However, Connectivity subscriber numbers missed at 13.6MM vs. 14.2MM expected, and the market's real focus is on Musk's call commentary around compute targets, a $100B ARR goal, new cloud contracts, Starlink Mobile, and potential Tesla combination.
SpaceX referenced an existing cloud services compute deal with Google, and investors will be watching for any update on the scope or expansion of that partnership on the earnings call.
Anthropic is cited as an existing SpaceX cloud compute customer. Any color on the size or renewal of that agreement could be a read-through for AI infrastructure demand.

SpaceX's Starlink Mobile ambitions are framed as a potential competitive threat to AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon, though skepticism remains high given spectrum constraints and the massive capex a nationwide network would require.

T-Mobile is named alongside AT&T and Verizon as an incumbent that Starlink Mobile could theoretically threaten, though the competitive risk is seen as limited given SpaceX's spectrum and financial constraints.

Verizon is included in the group of carriers facing potential long-term disruption from Starlink Mobile, with the caveat that most analysts remain skeptical of SpaceX's ability to execute a nationwide consumer wireless network.

Speculation about a SpaceX and Tesla combination has been circulating for some time and has intensified following the recent Roadster unveil, which incorporated SpaceX technology. Investors will be listening closely to Musk on the call for any commentary on a potential merger.

sectors: AI infrastructure and cloud compute remain in sharp focus given SpaceX's Super Intelligence segment growing 830% year-over-year. Telecom incumbents face a longer-term watch item around Starlink Mobile competitive risk, though near-term threat is seen as limited.

tts_summary: Here's what you need to know heading into the SpaceX earnings call. The headline numbers for the third quarter were genuinely impressive. Revenue came in at fourteen point six billion dollars, up a hundred and sixty-one percent year-over-year and well ahead of the Street's twelve point eight billion estimate. EBITDA hit eight point eight billion versus consensus of six point six billion. Every major segment beat — Space, Connectivity, and Super Intelligence — with Super Intelligence being the real standout, posting eight hundred and thirty percent revenue growth year-over-year. That acceleration was driven by new cloud services agreements, the acquisition of Cursor, and surging Grok adoption across enterprise and consumer customers. Compute capacity also continued to scale, ending the quarter at one point seven gigawatts, up from one point four in Q2. The one soft spot was Connectivity subscriber numbers, which came in at thirteen point six million versus the fourteen point two million the Street was looking for. ARPU was above plan at sixty-nine dollars versus the sixty-five dollar estimate, which softens the blow somewhat. Capex was right in line at nineteen point six billion for the quarter, with the vast majority — sixteen point four billion — going into the Super Intelligence business. Now here's the critical thing for today: the Q3 numbers are almost beside the point. What investors actually care about is what Elon Musk says on this call. There are five major topics the market will be hanging on. First, compute capacity targets — Musk has previously talked about hitting two gigawatts by year-end and ten gigawatts by the end of next year. Second, annualized recurring revenue — the company has telegraphed a goal of one hundred billion dollars in ARR by year-end, and the Street wants an update on progress. Third, cloud compute contracts — at the Goldman conference in September, the company disclosed it had signed a new compute deal beyond the existing agreements with Google and Anthropic, and investors want pipeline details. Fourth, Starlink Mobile — there is genuine hype around this becoming a major competitor to AT and T, T-Mobile, and Verizon, but significant skepticism remains given spectrum limitations and the enormous capital requirements for a nationwide network. And fifth, Tesla — chatter about a potential SpaceX and Tesla combination has been building, and the recent Roadster unveil, which incorporated SpaceX technology, has only added fuel to that speculation. Bottom line: the numbers give Musk a strong foundation to work from tonight. But the call, not the quarter, is the real event. Any disappointment on compute targets, ARR trajectory, or contract pipeline could easily overwhelm the earnings beat. Stay focused on the call.
